correctness.rationale: The quintic is geometrically smooth: its three partials have only sixteen possible simultaneous projective candidates, all rejected by direct substitution. Hence genus six. Two independently implemented exact finite-field enumeration algorithms reproduce N_1,...,N_6=(5,35,65,395,1025,3395). Newton identities and genus-six functional equation uniquely yield (1+3T^2+16T^4)^3. The irreducible ordinary quartic Frobenius factor and standard Honda–Tate/Tate theorems give A^3 over F4 and E^6 over F16; odd/even extension point formulas follow from roots. All supporting source programs are packaged and replayed.

value.rationale: The named curve is a geometrically natural and published smooth Frobenius-nonclassical genus-six quintic. Its Jacobian being an ordinary cube of a simple abelian surface over F4 and becoming sixfold elliptic over F16 is a structural arithmetic invariant, not an arbitrary unmotivated small count. Complete extension-point formulas, the splitting field for elliptic factors, and the ordinary Newton polygon make this exact computation valuable for understanding arithmetic behavior of this established special-geometry example. Claim does not assert new general Tate theory.
